question_text: What is the primary acceptor of CO2 in C4 plants? What is the first compound formed as a result of primary carboxylation in the C4 pathway?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The acceptor
steps.margin_note: Full name, carbon count, enzyme. The enzyme is worth adding.
lines: The primary acceptor of CO2 in C4 plants is
steps.why: PEP carboxylase has no affinity for oxygen at all, which is why a C4 plant can fix carbon without any photorespiration.
common_mistakes: Naming RuBP. RuBP is the C3 acceptor.
Saying the enzyme is RuBisCO. Primary carboxylation in C4 uses PEP CARBOXYLASE.
steps.memory_tip: PEP has three carbons and catches the fourth.

steps.label: The first compound
steps.margin_note: Mirror the C3 answer exactly: name, count, and the link to the pathway name.

lines.text: PEP (3C) catches CO2; OAA (4C) is what forms

lines: The first compound formed is OAA —
It is a 4-carbon compound, which is why the
pathway is called the C4 cycle.
steps.why: Three carbons plus one gives four, and the four-carbon product is what gives the pathway its name.
common_mistakes: Naming PGA. PGA is the first C3 product.
Leaving out the carbon count. Four carbons is why it is called C4.
steps.memory_tip: Four carbons in the first product names the C4 cycle.
